Verify that a set of cells belong to their commitments.

Each cell comes with a commitment, a cell index and a proof.

The proof shows that the cell holds the values of the committed polynomial on its coset.

The check is the universal verification equation of
<https://ethresear.ch/t/a-universal-verification-equation-for-data-availability-sampling/13240>.

It removes repeated commitments, then runs the core check.

The recovery uses FFTs, which is faster than Lagrange interpolation.

The method is the one of
<https://ethresear.ch/t/reed-solomon-erasure-code-recovery-in-n-log-2-n-time-with-ffts/3039>.

methods.summary: The public key grown from a seed.
methods.docstring:
The public key grown from a seed.

It builds the whole top tree, `2^16` one-time keys.

methods.summary: `Sig(sk, idx, m)` over a hash `H`: sign a message at a leaf index.
methods.signature: (seed: bytes, leaf_index: int, message: bytes) -> bytes
methods.docstring:
`Sig(sk, idx, m)` over a hash `H`: sign a message at a leaf index.

1. The scheme seed `S` and the public parameter `P`, from the secret key's seed.
2. The signature from `S` and `P`.

# Warning

Never sign two different messages at one leaf index with one secret key.

The top key `b` signs only the root of bottom tree `b`.

So it signs one message, however many leaf indices of that tree are used.

# Errors

- Either layer's one-time signature finds no codeword.

methods.summary: `Ver(pk, m, sigma)` over a hash `H`: whether a signature signs a message under a public key.
methods.signature: (public_key: bytes, message: bytes, signature: bytes) -> bool
methods.docstring:
`Ver(pk, m, sigma)` over a hash `H`: whether a signature signs a message under a public key.

A yes or a no, never a reason.

Which step rejected a well-formed signature carries no consensus meaning.

methods.summary: The leaf index a 2404-byte signature carries.
methods.docstring:
The leaf index a 2404-byte signature carries.

It reads only the first 4 bytes.

It does not verify the signature, so the index is only what the signer claims.

A caller can use it to require a given leaf before verifying.

For example, a proof of possession requires leaf 0.

methods.summary: The public key grown from a seed.
methods.docstring:
The public key grown from a seed.

It builds the whole top tree, `2^10` one-time keys.

methods.summary: `Sign(sk, m)`: sign a message.
methods.docstring:
`Sign(sk, m)`: sign a message.

1. The randomizer and the message give the digest: the index and one leaf per FORS tree.
2. FORS instance `idx` opens those leaves.
3. Each layer's key signs what the layer below gives, with its path.

# Warning

Never sign more than `2^30` messages with one secret key.

# Errors

- A one-time signature finds no codeword.

methods.summary: `Ver(pk, m, sigma)`: whether a signature signs a message under a public key.
methods.signature: (public_key: bytes, message: bytes, signature: bytes) -> bool
methods.docstring:
`Ver(pk, m, sigma)`: whether a signature signs a message under a public key.

A yes or a no, never a reason.

Which step rejected a well-formed signature carries no meaning for the caller.

methods.summary: SHA-256 of a byte string shorter than 2^61 bytes, the bound of FIPS 180-4 §1.
methods.docstring:
SHA-256 of a byte string shorter than 2^61 bytes, the bound of FIPS 180-4 §1.

A longer input wraps its bit length modulo 2^64, and the result is not SHA-256.

methods.summary: Keccak-256 of a byte string: `Keccak[512](M, 256)` of FIPS 202 §5.2.
methods.docstring:
Keccak-256 of a byte string: `Keccak[512](M, 256)` of FIPS 202 §5.2.

It absorbs at a rate of 136 bytes.

One block of output holds the 32 digest bytes, so no further permutation is needed.

methods.summary: Keccak-512 of a byte string: `Keccak[1024](M, 512)` of FIPS 202 §5.2.
methods.docstring:
Keccak-512 of a byte string: `Keccak[1024](M, 512)` of FIPS 202 §5.2.

It absorbs at a rate of 72 bytes, with the same permutation as Keccak-256.

One block of output holds the 64 digest bytes, so no further permutation is needed.

methods.docstring:
The bytes in the cache of the epoch of a block: `c_size` of the Yellow Paper, J.2.

The search starts one hash below the linear size.

methods.docstring:
The bytes in the dataset of the epoch of a block: `d_size` of the Yellow Paper, J.2.

The search starts one mix below the linear size.

methods.docstring:
The seed of the epoch of a block: `C_seedhash` of the Yellow Paper, J.3.1.

It is 32 zero bytes at epoch 0, and the Keccak-256 digest of the previous seed after.

methods.summary: The cache of the epoch of a block: `c` of the Yellow Paper, J.3.2.
methods.docstring:
The cache of the epoch of a block: `c` of the Yellow Paper, J.3.2.

It has one item per 64 bytes of the cache size, after three rounds over the initial cache.

methods.summary: The dataset item at an index, from the cache: `E_datasetitem` of the Yellow Paper, J.3.3.
methods.docstring:
The dataset item at an index, from the cache: `E_datasetitem` of the Yellow Paper, J.3.3.

The mix starts as the Keccak-512 digest of a cache item whose first word is XORed with the index.

Each of 256 parents is a cache item that the index and the mix choose, and FNV folds it in.

The item is the Keccak-512 digest of the last mix.

The appendix reads the cache by its size in bytes, and the specification by its count of items.

The definition follows the specification.

The index is below `2^32` while the dataset has fewer than `2^32` items.

methods.signature: (dataset_size: bytes, cache: bytes, header_hash: bytes, nonce: bytes) -> bytes

The 32-byte mix digest and the 32-byte result of the proof-of-work function, from a cache.

methods.docstring:
Keccak-f[1600], FIPS 202 §3.4: Keccak-p[1600, 24], rounds 0 to 23 in order.

With `n_r = 24 = 12 + 2l` the rounds run from `12 + 2l - n_r = 0` to `23` (§3.3, Algorithm 7).

methods.docstring:
The root of the trie that sets the pairs of `input` in order, from an empty trie.

The input is an RLP list of pairs, each a list of a key and a value.

An empty value removes its key.

A `secured` other than 0 hashes each key before it becomes a path.

The proof is an RLP list of byte strings, the encodings of the nodes.

No bytes means that `key` is not set, since no value is empty.

A root of another length than 32 bytes, or a proof that does not verify, is an error.

The hex-prefix encoding of a path, with one nibble in each input byte.

methods.signature: (public_key: bytes, msg_hash: bytes, signature: bytes) -> bool
methods.docstring:
Whether `(r, s)` is a valid signature on `hash` under the public key `q`, by SEC 1 v2 §4.1.4.

`q` must be a valid public key, as SEC 1 v2 §3.2.2.1 checks: on the curve, and not `O`.

A key from the decoder always is.

The key `O` would accept any `r` that some `u1 G` hits, so it is rejected here too.

methods.summary: The low-s rule of EIP-2: `s` is at most `n / 2`, rounded down.
methods.docstring:
The low-s rule of EIP-2: `s` is at most `n / 2`, rounded down.

Exactly one of `s` and `n - s` passes it, since `n` is odd.

methods.summary: The public key whose signature on `hash` is `(r, s)`, by SEC 1 v2 §4.1.6.
methods.signature: (msg_hash: bytes, signature: bytes, recovery_id: int) -> bytes
methods.docstring:
The public key whose signature on `hash` is `(r, s)`, by SEC 1 v2 §4.1.6.

The recovery id gives the parity of the `y` of `R`.

methods.summary: The signature `(r, s)` of a 32-byte hash, with its recovery bit, by SEC 1 v2 §4.1.3 and RFC 6979.
methods.docstring:
The signature `(r, s)` of a 32-byte hash, with its recovery bit, by SEC 1 v2 §4.1.3 and RFC 6979.

The low-s rule of EIP-2 replaces `s` by `n - s` when `s > n / 2`.

That signature rebuilds `-R`, so the recovery bit flips with it.

The key is secret, and this function makes no constant-time claim.

methods.summary: The shared secret of the private key `sk` and the public key `pk`, as 32 big-endian bytes.
methods.docstring:
The shared secret of the private key `sk` and the public key `pk`, as 32 big-endian bytes.

The public key must be on the curve and not `O`, as SEC 1 v2 §3.2.2.1 checks.

Step 2 rejects the point `O`, which a zero key gives.

The key is secret, and this function makes no constant-time claim.

methods.summary: The 20-byte Ethereum address of a private key.
methods.docstring:
The 20-byte Ethereum address of a private key.

It is the last 20 bytes of the Keccak-256 hash of the 64 bytes of `d G`.

The private key is secret, and EthLib makes no constant-time claim (SOUNDNESS.md A3).

methods.summary: Whether `(r, s)` is a valid signature on the hash integer `e` under the public key `q`.
methods.signature: (public_key: bytes, msg_hash: bytes, signature: bytes) -> bool
methods.docstring:
Whether `(r, s)` is a valid signature on the hash integer `e` under the public key `q`.

It is the verifying operation of SEC 1 v2 §4.1.4.

`e` acts mod `n`, like every scalar.

The signature is valid when `R = (e / s) G + (r / s) q` is not `O` and its `x` is `r` mod `n`.

methods.docstring:
Whether a record is a valid "v4" record: its signature verifies under its public key.

The signature is on the Keccak-256 hash of the RLP encoding of the content.

The RLP decoder accepts only canonical bytes, so for a decoded record this is what was signed.

ECDSA accepts a high `s` here, since the EIP adds no low-s rule.

The public key must be a point of the curve other than `O`, as for the ECDH of SEC 1 v2.

methods.signature: (fork: bytes, number: bytes, timestamp: bytes, parent_timestamp: bytes, parent_difficulty: bytes, parent_ommers: bytes) -> bytes
methods.docstring:
The difficulty of a block at a fork: `D(H)` of the Yellow Paper, 4.3.4, before Paris.

```text
    D(H) = max(D_min, P_d + ⌊P_d / 2048⌋ · factor + ε)
```

`P_d` is the parent's difficulty, and `ε` is the bomb.

The factor is the one of the time since the parent.

From Paris on, [EIP-3675](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#block-structure) sets it to 0.

The genesis block has no parent, and its difficulty is part of the chain's configuration.

methods.summary: Whether a node at a head accepts the fork identifier of a peer, by the validation rules of [EIP-2124](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2124#validation-rules).
methods.signature: (schedule: bytes, number: int, timestamp: int, remote: bytes) -> bool
methods.docstring:
Whether a node at a head accepts the fork identifier of a peer, by the validation rules of
[EIP-2124](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2124#validation-rules).

- 1: the two hashes match, so the nodes are at one fork.
  The node refuses only if it has passed the next fork that the peer announces (1a).
- 2: the hash of the peer is one of the node's earlier hashes, so the peer is syncing.
  The node accepts if the peer announces the fork that follows that hash, and refuses otherwise.
- 3: the hash of the peer is one of the node's later hashes, so the node is syncing, and it accepts.
- 4: the node refuses in every other case.

[EIP-6122](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6122#additional-rules) checks the forks by block
before the forks by time, as the order of the forks does.

The node compares its earlier hashes from the first one, so the first match decides rule 2.

methods.docstring:
The 64-bit value a varint denotes, or why it is not a valid varint.

The rules are checked in this order:

1. The ten-byte cap, while reading, so the work stays bounded.
2. Minimal encoding.
3. The 64-bit range.

# Why minimality is enforced

The specification only says SHOULD.

Rejecting padding means each length has exactly one encoding.

So a message cannot be re-sent with a different prefix that differs only in padding.

It reads the base fee per gas of the block, the gas left and the refund counter.

The base fee must be below 2^256, and 0 before London, which has none.

The price per gas must cover the base fee, and the gas left must be at most the gas limit.
